_note: Ground truth for CAD fixtures authored in Fusion, an independent kernel. These values were supplied with the parts rather than measured here, which is the point: reading them back is a check on this project's analyzer, not a rerun of whatever produced them. Lengths are millimetres, matching the SI_UNIT declaration in each file.

fixtureA.step.purpose: baseline, same shape as the build123d prototype, so the two kernels can be compared directly
fixtureA.step._edge_count_note: Fusion's UI reported 32; the B-rep holds 36 EDGE_CURVE entities. Faces agreed at 14, so again only the edge convention differs. The B-rep figure is the one tested, because the file declares it.

fixtureB.step.purpose: the trap: fillet radius equals hole radius, so a radius based rule merges eight cylinders into one group and only concavity separates them
fixtureB.step._edge_count_note: As with A and C, faces agreed (14) and only the edge convention differed: Fusion's UI reported 32, the B-rep holds 36 EDGE_CURVE entities. The B-rep figure is the one tested, because the file declares it.
fixtureB.step._transport_note: The base64 this file arrived in was corrupted in transit: in five places the byte sequence '.,5' or '.,6' had collapsed to a comma followed by that digit with its high bit set, losing one byte each. The file was 5 bytes short. It was repaired by inverting exactly that pattern, and the repair is trustworthy only because the md5 supplied with the file then matched: 3052b1cff32d9a30d12a68860f87903c. A repair that no checksum confirms would be an invented fixture, not a recovered one.
fixtureB.step._counterbore_convention: Decided for the counterbore case that is not yet a fixture: semantically a counterbore is ONE feature, the seat for a bolt head. The MVP single-face rules will report it as TWO concave cylinders, and that is a known gap, not a passing answer. Grouping coaxial cylinders with their annular shoulder into one feature needs adjacency reasoning and belongs to a later phase. Both numbers get recorded when that fixture arrives.

fixtureC.step.purpose: curved: a filleted rim produces a torus whose MINOR radius is the fillet radius. Also a second trap, because the body wall is a convex cylinder and must not be reported as a fillet
fixtureC.step._edge_count_note: Two different counts, both correct in their own terms. Fusion's UI reported 3; the B-rep holds 5 EDGE_CURVE entities, which is what the file itself declares and what an analyzer reading the file can check. The B-rep figure is the one tested. Faces agreed at 4, so only the edge convention differs.

fixtureD.step.purpose: a chamfer, which is a cone. The minimal pair against fixture C's toroidal rim fillet: same cylinder, same rim, blended one way and cut the other.
fixtureD.step._expectation: A chamfer is neither a hole nor a fillet under the MVP rules, so it must fall through to unclassified. Being claimed as a fillet would mean the tangency rule is wrong, since a 45 degree cone is not tangent to either neighbour. Recognising chamfers as such is later work; this fixture only asserts that the current rules do not invent a feature that is not there.
fixtureD.step.provenance: authored in Fusion, supplied with bytes and md5

fixtureE.step.purpose: the refutation: a fillet that is CONCAVE. An L bracket's reentrant corner blend is a concave cylinder, so it satisfies the old hole rule and the fillet rule at once.
fixtureE.step._what_it_refuted: Before this fixture the hole rule was 'concave cylindrical face'. That reported this fillet as a 10 mm diameter hole. Concavity cannot separate a bore from a reentrant blend, because both are concave.
fixtureE.step.provenance: authored in Fusion, supplied with bytes and md5

_counting_note: Topology counts are of DISTINCT entities. Walking a solid yields an edge once per face that uses it, so a naive traversal counts uses: this fixture gives 10 edge uses against 5 edges and 20 vertex uses against 3 vertices. The inflated numbers look entirely plausible, which is why a part with a known answer was needed to notice.

_hole_rule_history.rule_now: concave cylindrical face that wraps a full turn about its axis
_hole_rule_history.why_not_the_other_candidate: Both candidates, a full turn and an absence of tangent neighbours, separate all five fixtures correctly, so the fixtures could not choose between them. The full turn was chosen because it survives a case the fixtures do not yet contain: a bore whose mouth and whose bottom are both blended is tangent to two neighbours, which the tangency candidate would then call a fillet, while it remains a full turn and stays a hole. That reasoning is an argument, not a measurement, and it is untested until such a fixture exists.
_hole_rule_history.known_limit: A hole broken open by an intersecting feature no longer wraps a full turn and will not be reported as a hole. That is a real gap and is preferred to the alternative, since the alternative misreports ordinary blended holes.

prediction_for_a_bore_blended_at_both_en.written: before the fixture was received, so it can actually be wrong
prediction_for_a_bore_blended_at_both_en.predicted_because: the bore still wraps 360 degrees, so the committed rule keeps calling it a hole even though it now has two tangent neighbours
prediction_for_a_bore_blended_at_both_en.if_the_prediction_fails: the full turn choice was wrong and the rule needs replacing again, not patching to make this one fixture pass
